summary: Iteration 40 RETEST of HIGH-priority NotificationBell crash fix. The previously reported React 'NotFoundError: Failed to execute insertBefore' crash caused by nested <button> inside <button> is FIXED. Outer wrapper of each notification row is now <div role='button' tabIndex='0'> with onClick + onKeyDown(Enter/Space). Confirmed across all three roles (admin, sales, accounts): popover opens, row click deep-links to /customers/{id}?tab=notes&focus={fid} with no React error overlay; FollowUpTracker visible on landing; Done button completes the follow-up (toast appears, row disappears optimistically, NO unintended row navigation — e.stopPropagation works), keyboard Enter on focused row navigates same as click. Backend pytest /app/backend/tests/test_notification_bell.py: 11/11 PASS — no regression in GET /api/follow-ups/pending or PATCH /api/customers/{id}/follow-ups/{fid}. All TEST_ seed data on Ramya cleaned up.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix verified: NotificationBell.jsx L188-261 — outer row is now <div role='button' tabIndex={0}> with onKeyDown handling for Enter/Space. Inner Button (Done) coexists safely.
Minor (not blocking): file is ~272 lines, just over the 250 soft threshold flagged earlier. Consider extracting <NotificationItemRow /> into its own file when next touched.
Minor: NotificationBell still swallows fetch errors silently (`catch {}` on L64). Acceptable for logout flicker avoidance but a single console.warn on first failure would aid diagnostics.
Minor: 60s POLL_MS still hardcoded — consider moving to a constant export or env-driven feature flag if other components reuse polling.

rca_of_the_issue: Previous bug RCA stands: nested interactive <button> in <button> caused browsers to re-parent inner button at parse time, diverging React VDOM from real DOM; on unmount during route change, React's insertBefore against a stale sibling threw NotFoundError. Fix applied: outer wrapper changed to <div role='button' tabIndex={0}> with onKeyDown(Enter/Space) — keeps full a11y semantics, eliminates HTML nesting violation, and the post-navigation crash is gone (verified across admin/sales/accounts).
